scenes.title: The dependable one
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize the dependable person left with extra work Meet the book as an uneasy fictional voice Feel the narrator questioning the cost of kindness
scenes.composition: One worker remains after a meeting with unfinished tasks
addOrChange: Replace abstract motif and labels with a desk, departing colleague and three task sheets.

cues.narration: Everyone praises the dependable person, then leaves them with the unfinished work.
cues.visualAction: A colleague offers praise and leaves the extra papers behind.

cues.narration: The Last Naive Person turns that familiar moment into an uneasy philosophical fiction.
cues.visualAction: Hold on the remaining worker as the book is introduced.

cues.narration: Its narrator suspects that being kind can make you easy to use.
cues.visualAction: The worker looks toward the closed door before resuming work.

scenes.title: Virtue at work
scenes.viewerPurpose: Want to follow that doubt through ordinary life Notice that he also owes others kindness Expect his easy explanations to be challenged
scenes.composition: The narrator observes everyday generosity in a home and office
addOrChange: Add two short encounters and an open research book instead of floating keywords.

cues.narration: He follows that suspicion through family life, employment, faith, and our need to belong.
cues.visualAction: Move from a household favor to a workplace favor.

cues.narration: But he has benefited from someone else’s generosity too.
cues.visualAction: The narrator receives work another person completed for him.

cues.narration: Real research and imagined encounters keep challenging his most satisfying explanations.
cues.visualAction: Place a contrary observation beside his confident explanation.

scenes.title: When the observer chooses
scenes.viewerPurpose: Turn the suspicion back toward his own relationships Recognize the difference between being valued and being useful
scenes.composition: The narrator faces the person who helped him
addOrChange: Return to the shared table, avoiding the later committee scene or a moral verdict.

cues.narration: His sharpest questions come back to people who have been generous to him.
cues.visualAction: The narrator turns from his notes toward the generous colleague.

cues.narration: If you have ever confused being valued with being useful, this voice may stay with you.
cues.visualAction: End on the two people rather than the useful task.
